title: [20/04/2024] - Offices in Japan vs. in America
prompt: The diagrams below compare the layout of a typical Japanese office and a typical American office. Summarize the information by selecting and reporting the main features and make comparisons where relevant.

frame.name: Introduction
paragraphs: The diagrams show the different layouts of typical Japanese and American offices.

frame.name: Overview
paragraphs: Overall, the two office styles show contrasting approaches to workplace design, with the Japanese office featuring an open layout, while the American office consists of separate enclosed spaces. The Japanese design has a clear hierarchical arrangement, whereas the American layout divides the space into functional areas.

frame.name: Body 1
paragraphs: Looking at the Japanese office, the workspace uses an open-plan design with the department manager positioned at the top center. Two section managers are located on the left and right sides, each overseeing three rows of employee desks arranged in a grid pattern and organized in two equal columns. The whole office faces windows on the north wall, with the department manager's workspace aligned accordingly.

frame.name: Body 2
paragraphs: In contrast, the American office divides the space into areas with distinct functions. The right side contains private offices for managers, including separate rooms for two section managers and a department manager office at the bottom right. The center area has individual cubicles arranged in four rows, giving employees personal workspace. Meanwhile, the left side features functional rooms including a copy room at the top, a storage area, and two conference rooms at the bottom, all of which are adjacent to the west wall's windows.
